# Shared-Database / Astro Safety Checklist: Markdown CMS Website

**Purpose**: Validate that the database, auth and deploy requirements guarantee this feature cannot negatively affect the Astro site that shares the Supabase project.
**Created**: 2026-10-11
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md), [data-model.md](../data-model.md), [research.md](../research.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

**Focus**: Shared-database isolation (primary), plus security and migration safety. **Depth**: Standard. **Audience**: Author and reviewer, before `/speckit-tasks`.

**Re-scoped**: The design changed from a shared Supabase project (`cms_` tables) to an isolated project whose schema is Astro's baseline plus additive migrations (spec FR-026, research D3). Items CHK001–CHK027 are worded for the shared design; read "shared project" as "Astro's database during adoption" and `cms_` objects as "feature migrations". Most are now satisfied by the additive, rollback and rehearsal requirements (T006–T013); re-evaluate each against that reading. Nothing was deleted. On 2026-10-11 the owner waived CHK001–024 as superseded (no Astro data, accounts or project are shared) and reviewed and accepted CHK025–035.

## Schema Isolation

- [x] CHK001 (waived, superseded) Is the rule "this feature creates only `cms_`-prefixed objects and alters or drops nothing Astro owns" stated as a requirement, not only as a design choice? [Completeness, Spec §FR-012, Gap]
- [x] CHK002 (waived, superseded) Are all object kinds covered by the isolation rule (tables, functions, triggers, indexes, policies, grants, extensions, types)? [Coverage, Gap]
- [x] CHK003 (waived, superseded) Are the names of the shared objects reused (`administrator_profiles`, `is_administrator()`) listed explicitly, with a statement that they are used read-only and never modified? [Clarity, data-model.md]
- [x] CHK004 (waived, superseded) Is it specified that no trigger, policy or function created here can fire on, or be invoked against, Astro's `topics` or `content_items` tables? [Gap]
- [x] CHK005 (waived, superseded) Is the helper `cms_set_updated_at()` required to have a name that cannot collide with any Astro function, now and after Astro adopts embedded images? [Consistency, Spec §Assumptions]
- [x] CHK006 (waived, superseded) Are requirements defined for default privileges, so new `cms_` objects do not grant broader access than the narrow grants in the data model? [Gap, data-model.md §RLS]
- [x] CHK007 (waived, superseded) Is "never visible on the other site" defined in both directions, and does SC-008 say how it is measured? [Measurability, Spec §SC-008]

## Shared Administrator Arrangement

- [x] CHK008 (waived, superseded) Is a requirement stated that this feature never writes to `administrator_profiles`? [Gap]
- [x] CHK009 (waived, superseded) Are the expected results defined for when Astro changes the shape or semantics of `is_administrator()` or `administrator_profiles`? Is the dependency recorded as an assumption? [Dependency, Assumption]
- [x] CHK010 (waived, superseded) Is it clear that the same administrator account gets access to both sites, and is that accepted explicitly as a security trade-off? [Clarity, Spec §FR-012]
- [x] CHK011 (waived, superseded) Are Auth configuration changes limited, in the requirements, to adding a Redirect URL (no change to Astro's Site URL)? Is the failure mode for a mistake documented? [Completeness, research.md]

## Migration Safety

- [x] CHK012 (waived, superseded) Is it required that migrations are additive and re-runnable (idempotent) against the live shared project? [Gap]
- [x] CHK013 (waived, superseded) Is a rollback or removal requirement defined (a down script that removes only `cms_` objects)? [Recovery, Gap]
- [x] CHK014 (waived, superseded) Is the version-naming rule that avoids clashes with Astro's `0001`/`0002` stated as a requirement and not just as a research note? [Consistency, research.md]
- [x] CHK015 (waived, superseded) Are requirements defined for verifying a migration against a copy or local stack of Astro's schema before it runs on the shared project? [Coverage, Gap]
- [x] CHK016 (waived, superseded) Is the guarded local-only block that creates Astro prerequisites specified so that it provably cannot run on the hosted project? [Clarity, research.md]
- [x] CHK017 (waived, superseded) Is there a requirement to confirm that Astro's own existing tests still pass after the migrations are applied? [Measurability, Spec §SC-012]

## Access Control and Data Integrity

- [x] CHK018 (waived, superseded) Are the RLS rules for anon, authenticated non-administrators and administrators complete for select, insert, update and delete on both tables? [Completeness, data-model.md §RLS]
- [x] CHK019 (waived, superseded) Is it defined which "authenticated" users exist on the shared project (for example, Astro-only visitors), and that they get no write access here? [Coverage, Gap]
- [x] CHK020 (waived, superseded) Is the cascade delete of a topic's articles reconciled with Astro's `on delete restrict`, and is the difference stated so reviewers don't treat it as a conflict? [Conflict, data-model.md]
- [x] CHK021 (waived, superseded) Are the slug and `published_at` lock rules defined for bulk or direct SQL changes made outside the UI? [Edge Case, data-model.md]
- [x] CHK022 (waived, superseded) Is the `body` size limit (7,000,000) tied to a measured platform limit, given that the research could not confirm one? [Assumption, research.md §D6]
- [x] CHK023 (waived, superseded) Are the allowed embedded-image rules enforced at both the database and the sanitizer, with the same limits stated once? [Consistency, Spec §FR-004a-c]

## Shared Resource Load and Limits

- [x] CHK024 (waived, superseded) Are shared-project quotas (database size, bandwidth, request counts) considered, given that image-heavy articles are up to 7 MB each? [Gap, Non-Functional]
- [x] CHK025 Is it required that public list queries never fetch `body`, so Astro's performance is not affected by this site's traffic? [Measurability, contracts/data-access.md]
- [x] CHK026 Is the daily scheduled rebuild's database load quantified (number of requests per build)? [Clarity, Spec §FR-023]
- [x] CHK027 Is the fallback defined for the shared project becoming unavailable or rate-limited during the pre-render step? [Exception Flow, Spec §FR-024]

## Future Astro Adoption

- [x] CHK028 Are the compatibility requirements stated for when Astro later adopts embedded images (shared tables or separate ones; who migrates)? [Dependency, Spec §FR-022]
- [x] CHK029 Is it clear that the adoption guide and ready-to-file issue are deliverables with defined content, and that filing the issue is left to the user? [Completeness, Spec §FR-022]

## Adoption Path (added for the isolated-database design)

- [x] CHK030 Is it required that the baseline migrations are verbatim copies of Astro's and never edited? [Completeness, Spec §FR-026, data-model.md]
- [x] CHK031 Are required adoption migrations distinguished from optional behavior-changing ones (slug lock, body cap), with Astro able to adopt the former without the latter? [Clarity, Spec §FR-026]
- [x] CHK032 Is a rollback requirement defined that restores the exact baseline schema, and is it verified by the rehearsal? [Recovery, Spec §SC-014]
- [x] CHK033 Is it required that Astro-style inserts (without the new columns) keep working after adoption? [Coverage, tasks T012]
- [x] CHK034 Is the `published_at` backfill for already-active rows specified, including that it never alters other columns? [Clarity, data-model.md]
- [x] CHK035 Is it stated that no RLS policy or grant changes are needed for adoption, and is that verified? [Assumption, data-model.md §RLS]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`
- Add comments or findings inline
- Link to relevant resources or documentation
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference
